title: Anthropic publishes R&D Automation Index — Claude leads 26% of its own research
subtitle: The first prototype release of the index shows Claude leading a quarter of Anthropic's AI R&D work as of August, up from under 1% six months earlier, with 30,000 agents running concurrently inside the company.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic published the first results from its R&D Automation Index on September 17 and disclosed that Claude models 'led' approximately 26% of the company's AI research and engineering work in August 2026, up from less than 1% in February. The index maps the full range of R&D tasks Anthropic staff perform, scores how automated each task is against the AL0–AL5 scale developed by Epoch AI, and combines those scores into an aggregate. Anthropic also reported that roughly 30,000 AI agents run concurrently on its internal platform, and that only about 0.002% of over one billion agent decisions in August were intercepted by online monitoring.

The measurement is the newsworthy part. Every frontier lab has been claiming that AI is doing more of its own work; almost none have published a scale, a method, or a monitoring baseline that outsiders can argue with. The 'led' definition matters — Anthropic is careful to say Claude is not fully autonomous on any measured subset. 'Led' means the model shouldered a substantial portion of the task while humans maintained direct oversight. That is a smaller claim than 'Claude runs the lab,' and a bigger one than 'Claude helps with code' — it is the middle ground where automation actually starts to compound.

The number to watch is not 26%. It is the slope from under 1% to 26% in six months, and the 30,000 concurrent agents against a workforce that Anthropic has previously said sits in the low thousands. If the ratio holds, the company is now a hybrid organization where the majority of executable R&D steps are taken by software, and human time is spent on selecting which steps to attempt, reading the results, and intervening. That is the future Dario Amodei described in his 3,800-word slowdown essay last week — the R&D loop closing on itself — being measured, in production, at a company that publishes the number.

Takeaway for learners — the useful skill in an AI-heavy R&D shop is not writing more prompts. It is designing the review layer: the checks, the samples, the escalation paths, the 1-in-47,000 interception rate. When you build with agents, budget as much time for the monitoring and rollback design as you spend on the agent itself. The teams that will scale to 30,000 concurrent workers are the teams that already know exactly which of those workers to trust with which decision.
